reasoning: Select candidate TL-IN-76101000 based on product description matching aluminium window frames.
Verify that tariff line 76101000 is preferential under the India-UAE CEPA.
Identify MFN rate of 10% and 2026 CEPA preferential rate of 0% from TL-IN-76101000.
Evaluate origin against rule PSR-IN-R118 (CTSH + VA 45%), meeting all CTSH, VA (49.0% vs 45%), minimal operations, and final manufacture requirements.
Determine estimated duty saving of 10000.00 AED on the 100000 AED shipment value from TOOL:duty:76101000.
Detail procedural steps for claiming preference, including factory registration, e-service application, fee payment, issuing timeframe, direct consignment, importer filing, and record keeping.
Compile caveats regarding CIF valuation, duty scope, self-declaration reliance, issuing authority naming, and free-zone eligibility.

classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: Final manufacture in UAE check passed; minimal operations check passed; CTSH check passed (all 3 non-originating inputs classified outside subheading 761010); VA build-down passed at 49.0% against threshold of 45% on FOB basis (6 total inputs, 3 non-originating inputs, non-originating share 51%).

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires factory registration prior to application, which mandates the factory to be located outside a free zone and hold a MoIAT industrial licence with a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter applies for the certificate through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service on moet.gov.ae by uploading the commercial invoice and proof of factory registration.
Pay the certificate fee of AED 50 to the Ministry of Foreign Trade for invoice values up to AED 100000.
The competent authority issues the Certificate of Origin prior to, at, or within five (5) working days of the date of exportation.
The exporter ensures direct consignment of the shipment from the UAE to India.

The Indian importer claims the preferential tariff treatment when filing the bill of entry and maintains CAROTAR 2020 origin details; electronic certificates are reportedly uploaded to e-Sanchit (unconfirmed: seen only in secondary sources).
The exporter must retain all origin and cost records for at least five (5) years starting from the end of the year of certificate issuance.

caveats.note: No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Free-zone producers are likely not eligible for Factory Registration required prior to obtaining a certificate of origin.
